questions.question:
Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blank.

By this time next week, we _______ Shimla.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is that **'will have reached'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **"By this time"** is a prepositional phrase that is used for a situation or event that has already happened or occurred

 
 
• **By this time** generally goes with **Future Perfect Tense**.

 
 
• ** Example:** ***By this time*** next week, Priyanka will have left for her trip.
 
 
 
 
 
• With the above example, we can say that **option 1 **is the correct answer.
 
• **Correct Sentence**: By this time next week, we ***will have reached*** Shimla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Perfect Tense**: The future perfect tense is for talking about an action that will be completed between now and some point in the future.
 
• The **Structure** of Future perfect tense**: will have + [past participle].**
 
 
• **​For example: **Linda ***will have left*** before you get there.

questions.question:
The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.

She didn't thank you for your help, but she may have done it.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** "may have done it".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **In the first part of the given sentence, **'didn't**' is used which shows that the sentence is in the** simple past tense**.
 
• Following the **Rule of Parallelism in tenses,__** the verbs used in a sentence that has the **same subject** should be having the **same tense**.
 
• **She **is a common subject in the whole sentence.
 
• So, instead of **"may"** we need to use **'might'**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

**__Correct Sentence__: ***She didn't thank you for your help, but she** might** have done it.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blank.

Please go with ________ sister to the match.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Me and My.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the above sentence, we can say that the phrase conveys that which is acted upon, the object in the sentence. Here **"sister"** is an **object.**
 
• When a **noun or pronoun** works as an object in the sentence, an **objective case appears.**
 
 
• **​Example: ***Ajinkya told me that news.*
 
 
 
• Here, we need an objective case after the verb **go**. **'Me'** is the only objective case here.
 
• Now, **my** is followed by the noun, here the noun is 'Sister'. 
 
• Hence,** " me and my"** are the appropriate words to fill in the blank.
 
• The correct answer is **option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• **"My and Mine" :** 
 
• Use** ‘my’** before the word, and use **‘mine’** after the word. Remember **‘my’** is always followed by a noun, whereas **'mine'** replaces the noun.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'​While'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence " (2) _______ school are preparing themselves to restart, most parents are still not sure of sending their (3) ______ to school". Conveys 2 different scenarios where both clauses are contradicting each other.
 
• ** While** is a** ****subordinating conjunction.**
 
• ** **A subordinating conjunction is a** word or phrase**' that links a **dependent clause** to an **independent clause.**
 
• Generally, the two clauses that we use in sentences that start with “**while**” will **contradict __**each other.
 
• They will add different groups of information to the overall sentence to help us understand what someone is doing or saying.
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate word to fill in the blank is **'While'.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

__So the complete passage is- __*According to a news report, schools are setting up adequate facilities and taking (1) steps to restart learning on campus hoping to reopen schools later, if not sooner. (2) while schools are preparing themselves to restart, most parents are still not sure of sending their (3) children to school. Parents of primary school children are particularly concerned about their children's (4) exposure to health risks. Parents, in general, say that they have always tried to keep their children away from (5) devices like mobile phones and tablets, but the current Covid-19 situation has forced the children into online learning, and they spend long hours in front of screens.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence "***Parents of primary school children are particularly concerned about their children's (4) _______ to health risks***." is saying about the parents of primary school children who are concerned about their children's vulnerability to health hazards.
